narrative: OMX30 opens with conflicting signals: European bourses (DAX +0.13%, FTSE +0.58%) and modest commodity recovery (copper +0.60%, gold +0.41%) provide tailwinds, but NASDAQ weakness (-0.44%), Asia selloff (Nikkei -1.82%), and MACD bearish crossover create friction. The index remains firmly above its 200-MA (+4.6%) in bull-mode structurally, but weak ADX (5.4) with bearish DI bias signals low conviction and mean-reversion risk—RSI at 45 is neutral but offers room to both sides. US 10Y yield compression (-1.01%) is a mixed signal: bullish for growth but slightly negative for bank NIM expansion. Oil's 1.62% drop eases input costs but reduces upstream upside. Expect a choppy, low-volume Tuesday consolidation near 3123 (yesterday close).
morningBrief: OMX30 faces a muddy open on Tuesday 13 Oct. Europe is firm, but Asia's Nikkei crash (-1.82%) and US tech rout (-0.44% NASDAQ) create cross-currents. Weak ADX (5.4) means reduce conviction by 30%—we're in a no-trend environment; treat support at 3085 (lower Bollinger) and resistance at 3180 (50-MA) as tactical ranges, not conviction calls. USD/SEK at 9.975 (+0.13%) supports exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), but NASDAQ sell-off weighs on Ericsson and Hexagon sentiment. Oil down helps industrials' margins but crimps materials upside. Banks neutral—yield compression offsets NIM benefit. Boliden worth a watch on copper strength (+0.60%) and gold resilience. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET as a potential volatility trigger. Stay nimble; trend is weak, mean-reversion risk elevated.
